欢迎来到sprawling v0.0.14 Alpha 261027 (STILL WALKING)！
这个版本约等于v0.0.13.1，但就这样了。今天发现了一些小问题顺带解决一下，比如[#205](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/pull/205)修掉了composer权限弹层和地址行重叠、导致控件被遮挡和点击被截获的问题。这一版没有改变wire或已保存数据格式。项目的开发前期主要使用Claude Opus5，近期改为Claude Opus5.5，有些事情的处理我有点过度依赖Claude以至于讲的不是很清楚而实现方式和效果也不是每一次Claude都可以完美读懂或做出了我满意的结果（当然相比于其他模型Claude在这个方面有着不止一代的差距），这一版的修复主要使用Kimi K3.1 Pro，我把实现方式和细节、必要的验收条件和关键约束都讲细了一点，问题大概得到了解决，同时随着Bun1.4.4的发布同步加入了bun fmt作为检查矩阵的一环。
现在越来越多的功能实现可以使用MCP，不再都需要在核心做插件或者预留接口，但“支持MCP”和“完整的QQBot”不是一回事：对sprawling来说，MCP工具不会自行把一条新QQ消息派进城市，持续接收、路由和回复仍要由外部桥、客户端或其他入口承担。比如[#80](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/issues/80)谈到的[OneBot](https://github.com/botuniverse/onebot)方案，可以由[NapCatQQ](https://github.com/NapNeko/NapCatQQ)或[SnowLuma](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma)提供QQ协议接入，NapCatQQ自己的README目前也推荐SnowLuma作为NapCat Gui的替代品；从我身边不少开发者的实际反馈来看，SnowLuma在稳定性上也确实更好一些。qq-bridge则通过SnowLuma接收QQ消息并接入DeepSeek Harness，同时用MCP提供部分QQ工具；即使走这条路线，持续接入仍由SnowLuma和桥接进程承担，MCP只负责其中的一部分。若只需要Agent主动查询或发送消息，MCP已经很够用；需要双向持续接入时可以选择外部桥，computer use直接操控桌面端也能覆盖一部分场景；最后仅用于私聊做人机恋、生活管家或远控替代方案的话，QQ开发平台可能更合适，[官方文档](https://bot.q.qq.com/wiki/develop/api-v2/server-inter/message/type/markdown.html)目前支持单聊和群聊的自定义Markdown消息。所以我个人感觉也许接下来的开发应该专注于继续性能优化，微调一些前端细节以及为一些有趣的实践提供空间。人们使用Agent的方式差别很大，有很多即使是大学里的学生也才刚刚开始接触Agent，更别说世界上其他的大部分甚至没接触过前沿AI或者没意识到生活中有AI。面向那些最前沿的高AI消费用户去设计可以提前预知需要哪些功能，而面向更广大用户的真实场景设计才能确保设计出的内容“实用”。其实很多实用的功能并不实用，比如说全屋智能家居控制这件事就得要要求先有个房子然后全屋安装智能家居，这个功能大部分人都用不上，而实际需要的人中的大部分需求都可以依靠MCP和phone use或者写脚本解决。“人们”的生活很贫瘠、空虚，反倒是用于娱乐的功能会在传播和使用上超过那些生产用功能。我们当然不该说这些娱乐的功能更重要，而且也没必要专门在一个泛用的框架中专门实现它（所以我没有为一个细枝末节的功能专门实现一个包塞到项目里面），只要核心功能更加鲁棒这些功能就会随着模型的进步和人们的发现更好地完成。 <!-- lexicon-ok: the author's own word in his release note, quoted and not changed -->
用长期主义的观点来看待这个项目吧，以能接受的速度稳步推进，长期维护一个至少自己愿意长期使用的项目才是短期目标。

**In English / 英文版**

Welcome to sprawling v0.0.14 Alpha 261027 (STILL WALKING)!

This release is roughly v0.0.13.1, but that is what it is. I found a few small problems today and fixed them along the way; for example, [#205](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/pull/205) fixes the composer's permissions popover overlapping the address line, which obscured the control and intercepted its clicks. This release changes neither the wire nor the saved-data formats. Early development used mostly Claude Opus 5, and more recently Claude Opus 5.5. In some places I relied too much on Claude: I did not explain things clearly enough, and Claude did not always perfectly understand the implementation and the effect I wanted, or produce a result I was satisfied with (although, in my experience, Claude is more than a generation ahead of other models in this respect). Most of the fixes in this release used Kimi K3.1 Pro. I spelled out the implementation, the details, the necessary acceptance criteria and the key constraints more carefully, and the problems were more or less resolved. With Bun 1.4.4 released, `bun fmt` also joined the check matrix.

More and more features can now be implemented through MCP, so not every one needs a plugin in the core or an interface reserved for it. But “supporting MCP” and “being a complete QQ bot” are not the same thing. For sprawling, an MCP tool does not spontaneously deliver a new QQ message into the city: sustained receiving, routing and replies still need an external bridge, a client or another entrance. Take the [OneBot](https://github.com/botuniverse/onebot) approach discussed in [#80](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/issues/80): [NapCatQQ](https://github.com/NapNeko/NapCatQQ) or [SnowLuma](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma) can provide the QQ protocol connection, and NapCatQQ's own README now recommends SnowLuma as a replacement for NapCat Gui. Feedback from quite a few developers around me also says that SnowLuma is more stable in practice. qq-bridge receives QQ messages through SnowLuma and connects them to DeepSeek Harness, while exposing some QQ tools through MCP; even on this route, SnowLuma and the bridge process carry the sustained connection, and MCP handles only one part. If you only need an Agent to query or send messages actively, MCP is already enough; for sustained two-way integration, you can choose an external bridge, and computer use driving the desktop client directly can cover some scenarios too. Finally, if the goal is only private-chat human–AI relationships, a life assistant or a substitute remote-control channel, QQ's official developer platform may be a better fit: its [official documentation](https://bot.q.qq.com/wiki/develop/api-v2/server-inter/message/type/markdown.html) currently supports custom Markdown messages in one-to-one and group chats. So I now think perhaps the next development work should focus on further performance optimisation, small frontend refinements, and leaving room for interesting experiments. People use Agents in very different ways: many university students have only just started using them, let alone most people elsewhere in the world, who may never have used frontier AI or noticed the AI already present in their lives. Designing for the most advanced, highest-consuming AI users can tell you in advance which features will be needed; designing for the real situations of a much wider range of people is what makes the result “useful”. Many supposedly useful features are not actually useful. Whole-home smart control, for example, first requires you to have a home and then fill it with smart devices. Most people cannot use that at all, and most of the needs of those who do can be met with MCP, phone use or a script. “People's” lives are sparse and empty; features for entertainment will spread and be used more than features for production. That does not mean entertainment features are more important, and there is no need to implement each one in a general-purpose framework (which is why I did not add a package to the project for one minor feature). As long as the core becomes more robust, people and better models will find ways to do these things well.

Let us take a long-term view of this project: move forward steadily at a pace I can accept, and maintain over the long term a project that at least I myself am willing to keep using; that is the short-term goal.

**Notes / 补充**

- **Known issue / 已知问题** — ([#185](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/issues/185)) On an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, forking a session containing tool calls fails. The Ledger redacts the provider's tool call id as `secret:redacted/<hash>` because of its key-like shape, and the rebuilt history sends it back unchanged; Anthropic requires an id matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, answers 400, and the run ends cancelled. Version 0.0.13 behaves the same way, and the proposed fix in [#189](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/pull/189) is not included in this release. An OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepts the id, and a new session is unaffected.

  （[#185](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/issues/185)）在 Anthropic 兼容格式的端点上，分叉一个含工具调用的会话会失败。账本把 provider 给的 tool call id 按密钥形状抹成 `secret:redacted/<hash>`，重建历史时原样发出，Anthropic 要求 id 匹配 `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`，回答 400，run 以 cancelled 结束。0.0.13 也是这样；[#189](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/pull/189) 的候选修复没有包含在本版中。OpenAI 兼容格式的端点接受这个 id，新会话不受影响。

**What comes next** — continued performance work, small frontend refinements, and more room for interesting experiments through MCP, scripts and external clients. No version or date is promised for `v0.1.0` Beta, and finishing any item here does not by itself make it.
